title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - Preventing Human Trafficking
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Enacting strict anti-trafficking laws and establishing law enforcement agencies to prosecute traffickers is categorized under which preventive measure?
questions.explain: **Legislation** involves the creation and enforcement of strict laws by the government to serve as a deterrent and strictly punish offenders.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) prints posters, broadcasts radio jingles, and distributes flyers to inform the general public about the tricks used by human traffickers, they are engaging in:
questions.explain: Using mass media, posters, and flyers to rapidly spread information and alert the public about the dangers of a phenomenon constitutes an **awareness campaign**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: How does **Education** serve as a long-term preventive measure against human trafficking?
options: It teaches students how to legally smuggle goods across borders
It empowers citizens with knowledge, critical thinking, and employability skills to escape poverty
It provides traffickers with better routes to transport victims
It forces children to leave their families to live in schools permanently
questions.explain: **Education** eliminates ignorance and provides individuals with marketable skills, thereby significantly reducing poverty and vulnerability to traffickers' deceitful promises.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which preventive measure involves individuals or groups continuously pleading, speaking up, and lobbying government authorities to implement better policies protecting vulnerable women and children?
questions.explain: **Advocacy** is the active support of an idea or cause, which includes lobbying policymakers and speaking out on behalf of vulnerable groups to bring about systemic change.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: In Nigeria, the agency primarily established through *legislation* to fight against human trafficking and prosecute offenders is known by the acronym NAPTIP. What does it stand for?
options: National Association of Patriotic Traders and International Partners
National Agency for Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons
Nigerian Authority for Prevention of Trafficked Infants and Parents
National Action against Prostitution and Trafficked Innocent Persons
questions.explain: NAPTIP stands for the **National Agency for Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons**, which represents a major legislative milestone in Nigeria's fight against human trafficking.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If schools incorporate topics detailing the dangers of trafficking into their Social Studies syllabus (just like this BECE curriculum), this is a practical example of utilizing which preventive measure?
questions.explain: Teaching the subject systematically in schools to equip youths with knowledge is a direct application of **Education** as a preventive tool.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the preventive measures for human trafficking as stated in the syllabus?
options: Legislation, Awareness campaign, Advocacy, and Education
Divorce, Constant fighting, and Broken homes
questions.explain: The syllabus outlines preventive measures as **Awareness campaign, Education, Advocacy, and Legislation**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Why must **Legislation** be complemented by **Law Enforcement** to effectively prevent human trafficking?
options: Because laws on paper are useless if there are no agencies to catch and punish the offenders
Because law enforcement agencies only exist to protect the traffickers
Because passing laws automatically guarantees that criminals will stop their activities immediately
Because legislation can only be passed by police officers
questions.explain: **Legislation** provides the legal framework (the rules and punishments), but it requires active law enforcement agencies to execute the laws, make arrests, and prosecute traffickers.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: A traditional ruler organizes a town hall meeting to warn parents about strangers who offer to take their children to the city for "free schooling." What preventive strategy is the ruler employing?
questions.explain: The ruler is creating **awareness** about the danger while also playing an **advocacy** role by counseling the community to protect their children.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: The phrase "Trafficking in persons is a crime against humanity" is often used during public rallies to demand harsher government actions. This rally acts as both an awareness campaign and:
questions.explain: Public rallies demanding policy changes from the government (harsher actions) are a classic form of **advocacy**, pleading the cause of victims at a systemic level.

questions.subject: National Values Education
